name: Rudianus

attributes.attribute: an obscure Continental Celtic god in France
identified by Romans with the warrior Mars
his name is invoked at three places in southern France
the stone of Saint-Michel-de-Valbonne shows a horseman carrying five severed heads

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rudianus is a Continental Celtic god of war. He is a dim figure known only from a few stones in France that called on his help. Romans linked him with their warrior god Mars. His name appears at three places in southern France. At Saint-Michel-de-Valbonne a stone cuts the figure of a horseman. He rides with five severed heads. That image fits a war-god of grim repute.

okr.objective: Present Rudianus as a shadowy war-god of southern Gaul.
key_results: Count the three places in southern France that invoke him
Record the horseman with five severed heads at Saint-Michel-de-Valbonne
